October 2026 • Issue #7
From the Desk of Product

October felt like the month we finally stopped talking about the data and started using it. The Clinical Intelligence Dashboard is live, LucinaCare is around the corner, and somewhere in between, we learned that duplicates belong in photo albums — not databases. Welcome to Issue #7.

Product Updates

What we shipped

Clinical Intelligence Dashboard

After a three-month pilot, the Clinical Intelligence dashboard launched GA on 10/16 for all affiliates and user groups!

The dashboard groups a 10-pack of quality and P4P metrics across OB and GYN into a single view, with the option to drilldown to view details on specific metrics, care centers, providers, and patients.

Line of sight into this data is imperative given the quality metrics impact patient outcomes, and the P4P measures impact affiliate reimbursements and statuses with payers. This dashboard consolidates several bespoke excel or PBI reports used by affiliates today, providing a single source of truth for these imperative analytics, used by clinical quality partners, program managers, analytics partners and medical directors.

Throughout the pilot phase, user discovery sessions with each affiliate validated trust in the data, workflow fit, and risk in relying on the data, as well as additional functionality. Based on this feedback and requests, the GA release included multiple new features.

Three new features included in GA:

1. Care Center Detail for a holistic view of specific care center performance against all measures, with provider and patient level details

2. Patient-level views of metric compliance with associated provider and care center views

3. Affiliate filtering to toggle between affiliates for those with access to multiple affiliates or markets

Engagement in the first two days is trending well, with 19 of 39 users accessing the dashboard, with an average of 7 pages viewed per session. Initial feedback is also encouraging: “FIRST OF ALL!!! WOW. This is REALLY coming along.” - Director of Quality and Healthcare Solutions

We'll continue to collect feedback through the embedded form and iterate on enhancements as engagement expands. Both near and longer term goals include embedding NextGen and eCW data, ingesting next appointment dates for patient rosters, layering in specific care center metric targets.

Reach out to Clayton or Ashley with any questions or ideas!

What's Next

Looking ahead

LucinaCare Enablement Phase 1 Release • November 6

We are releasing the first set of Discover updates to support LucinaCare case management in Discover on November 6. These changes help care teams see which members are part of the program and manage who owns each case.

Questions or feedback? Reach out to the Ashley or Lindsay.

  • Engaged Status: Case owners can now move a member to a new Engaged status once they’ve chosen to enter the care management program.
  • SMI Condition Flag: The Severe Mental Illness (SMI) condition now carries a flag in the Conditions module on the Member Profile, so you can spot an SMI diagnosis at a glance.
  • LucinaCare Badge: A new badge in the main grid and Member Profile shows which episodes are part of the LucinaCare program, so you don’t have to open each case to find out.
  • Case Owner Transfer: You can now assign or reassign an episode to a new case owner directly from the Member Profile.

Get to Know the Team

Priyanka Awate — Data Engineer - Kanini

Hi, I'm Priyanka! I'm a Python Developer with over 5 years of experience, mainly working with Python, PySpark, Databricks, and data engineering.

I enjoy solving challenging problems, optimizing data pipelines, and finding ways to make processes simpler and more efficient. I believe there's always something new to learn in technology, and that's what keeps my work interesting.

Outside of work, I enjoy spending time with my family, traveling to new places, and relaxing with a good cup of coffee. I also love exploring new foods, especially desserts!

Which data smell is most offensive?

Duplicate records with no dedup logic — because duplicates belong in photo albums, not in databases! 😄

Pick your villain:

The pipeline that only breaks in production — because it works perfectly everywhere, except where it actually matters! 😂
